analysis.title: Weekly power brief #84: 3Q preview – From backlogs to bottom lines (Transformational Innovation Opportunities (TRIO): Power and resources)
key_insights: UBS CIO expects broadly supportive 3Q26 results for the Power and resources strategy. Structural demand from data centers, power generation, grids and electrification remains in place, with upside from an improving automation cycle and stronger metals prices.
The investment debate is shifting from the strength of demand, which is no longer in question, to how efficiently companies convert demand into earnings growth and cash flow.

UBS stays constructive but more selective. It prefers companies with visibility, execution credibility and balance-sheet strength, and avoids those whose valuations leave little room for disappointment.
Post-earnings price action is expected to depend on guidance quality amid a volatile macro environment, not on the headline results.

For electrical equipment suppliers the key tests are backlog quality, delivery cadence, pricing and incremental margins. For utilities they are load growth, capital plans, financing needs and regulatory recovery. For copper and aluminum miners they are operational execution, cost inflation and capital allocation.

In the week ending 16 October the Power and resources strategy posted negative absolute returns and underperformed the MSCI ACWI. Concerns over funding of the AI buildout hit data center infrastructure names. Equipment and facilitator stocks fell most, utilities and materials outperformed, and US names lost the most.

US industrials: intra-quarter primary research points to another quarter of solid organic growth and margin expansion. The open question is whether order growth can outpace already-strong revenue growth and whether incremental margins hold amid supply constraints and rising input costs.
UBS says the recent derating in industrial valuations provides some cushion ahead of results, although investor expectations are likely high.

UBS will press management on the backlog mix between firm, funded projects and those dependent on future permitting or grid interconnection, given concerns that power constraints could delay revenues.

Schneider Electric 3Q organic growth was 16.9%, with Energy Management up 18.8% and Industrial Automation up 8.1%. Data-center demand grew at a triple-digit rate, with improving visibility into 2027 and 2028, and Schneider upgraded its 2026 financial target.
UBS expects strong results from Legrand, Prysmian, Siemens Energy and Siemens. Prysmian could raise FY26 guidance, and fibre-optics and data-center trends offer upside to 2027 estimates.
Siemens Energy's debate is shifting from order growth to cycle duration and margin conversion. The November capital markets day could lift 2030 margin ambitions and shareholder returns.

Capacity and supply-chain bottlenecks are a greater constraint than any saturation in end demand. Short-cycle indicators remain in expansionary territory and have strengthened in some countries, which supports the automation recovery.
Siemens combines structural strength in Smart Infrastructure with potential upside from a Digital Industries recovery, and Schneider's results are a positive read-across for both.

Utilities enter the season with favorable volumes but a more demanding financing environment. Consensus points to y/y sector earnings growth led by independent power and renewable producers, while regulated utilities benefit from rising grid investment and load forecasts.

NextEra reported strong 3Q26 results at FPL and NextEra Energy Resources, with a growing renewables and storage backlog. It reiterated its long-term adjusted earnings and dividend growth targets and described a multi-gigawatt pipeline of large-load projects from data centers.

Liberty Energy (LBRT) reported improved 3Q26 operations on higher completion activity and service pricing. It signed a multi-gigawatt power development agreement with a frontier AI lab and an infrastructure partner, with a significant upfront capacity fee prepayment and energization targeted from late 2027. UBS reads this as positive for Solaris (SEI).
Copper and aluminum miners get a revenue tailwind from higher prices, but dispersion after earnings should depend on production volume, unit costs, energy exposure and capital allocation.

UBS used the selloff in industrials and utilities, which it calls largely non-fundamental, to add higher-beta holdings Forgent Power Solutions and Solaris Energy Infrastructure to the Power and resources list.

sector_views.sector: Power and resources (electrical equipment, utilities, copper and aluminum miners)
sector_views.rationale: Highly constructive but increasingly selective. Structural demand from data centers, grids and electrification is intact, and UBS favors visible backlogs, disciplined balance sheets and margin protection.
Strong demand and backlog conversion support growth and margin expansion. Capacity and supply chains are the constraint.
Favorable load growth and grid investment, but financing is more demanding. UBS favors high-quality utilities.
Higher prices help, with copper supported by tight mine supply and electrification demand and aluminum by supply discipline. UBS favors low-cost producers.

earnings_insights: Schneider Electric 3Q26 reported: revenue EUR 11.5B, up 17% organically (16.9% organic per UBS text), Energy Management +18.8% organic, Industrial Automation +8.1% organic, data-center demand up triple digits, record backlog, 2026 financial target upgraded (reported 16 Oct 2026).

NextEra Energy 3Q26 reported strong financial and operational performance at FPL and NextEra Energy Resources. It reiterated long-term adjusted EPS and dividend growth targets. The note gives no EPS figures.

Liberty Energy 3Q26 reported improved operating results on higher completion activity and service pricing. It signed a multi-gigawatt power agreement with an upfront capacity fee prepayment and targeted energization from late 2027.
Expected, not yet reported: Prysmian could raise FY26 guidance. UBS expects strong results from Legrand, Prysmian, Siemens Energy and Siemens.
Siemens Energy's capital markets day in November is a catalyst for higher 2030 margin ambitions and shareholder returns.

trade_ideas.description: Add higher-beta holdings Forgent Power Solutions and Solaris Energy Infrastructure to the Power and resources equity preference list
trade_ideas.rationale: UBS views the derating in industrials and utilities as largely non-fundamental and used the selloff to add them.
trade_ideas.risk: Forgent: demand slowdown, inability to fill new capacity, limited public track record. Solaris: project execution, local permitting and financing.

risk_factors: AI buildout funding concerns and a possible slowdown in data center capex.
Order normalization after exceptional growth, project delays, labor bottlenecks, unfavorable mix and renewed material-cost pressure.
Power constraints delaying revenues, and backlog dependent on permitting or grid interconnection.
Higher interest rates, input costs and a financing burden for utilities.
Valuations that leave little room for disappointment.
Macro downturn, China slowdown (Anglo American, copper and aluminum demand) and commodity price declines.
Regulatory, wildfire and storm risk for regulated utilities.
vol_and_positioning: The Power and resources strategy underperformed the MSCI ACWI in the week ending 16 October after AI buildout funding concerns hit data center infrastructure names.
UBS views the recent derating in industrials and utilities as largely non-fundamental and used it to add higher-beta names.
geopolitical: Further escalation of US-China tensions is listed as a risk for Zhongji Innolight.

tension_points.bull_case: Data-center and electrification demand is strong and broad-based, with Schneider data-center demand up triple digits, record backlogs and improving visibility into 2027 and 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Order normalization, project delays, labor bottlenecks, power constraints delaying revenues and AI funding concerns could disappoint, and valuations leave little room for error.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Order normalization after a period of exceptional growth, or a slowdown in data center capex.

theme_stances.key_argument: Demand for data center power systems, transmission and distribution equipment remains strong, and the debate is shifting to converting demand into earnings and cash flow.
theme_stances.evidence: We remain highly constructive, but increasingly selective.

theme_stances.key_argument: Higher prices help, but post-earnings dispersion depends on volume, unit costs, energy exposure and capital allocation.
theme_stances.evidence: unlikely to be a simple commodity-price story
